metadata.content:
Current task: Validate your guardrail + confirm your workflow is now correct and safe

✅ What you did right (no fluff)


You stopped forcing main → correct (GitHub blocked you anyway)


You moved to a feature branch → correct


You merged main into your branch (NOT rebase) → correct


You used --ours to preserve stable builder → correct


You committed + pushed feature branch → correct


You created kpush automation → strong move (this eliminates human error)



⚠️ One issue you hit (and why)
This error at the end:
zsh: parse error near `\n'
Cause:

You pasted raw guardrail text directly into terminal. Bash tried to execute it as code.
Fix: never paste plain text into terminal unless it's a script.

🔧 What your setup now actually does
Your kpush script enforces:


No commits on main ✔


Always merges latest main ✔


Stops on conflicts ✔


Forces safe push flow ✔


This replaces 90% of your manual Git mistakes.

⚠️ Critical reality (don’t ignore this)
Your guardrail is solid, but this line is dangerous if abused:
git checkout --ours <file>
This means:
👉 You are discarding remote changes completely
That is only safe because:


You intentionally treat your builder state as source of truth


You are prioritizing stability over merging logic


If you misuse this → you can silently delete important updates

🔒 Final hardened version (small improvement only)
Add this rule mentally:
ONLY use --ours for:


builder UI


preview engine


AI routes you just stabilized


NEVER use --ours for:


auth


billing


infra configs


environment files



✅ Answer to your implicit question

“Do I still need guardrails if I have kpush?”

Yes — but for different reasons:


kpush = execution safety


Guardrail = decision safety


Without guardrail → you still break architecture

Without kpush → you still break Git
You need both.

📍 Status


Git workflow: SAFE


Branch strategy: CORRECT


Conflict strategy: CONTROLLED


Automation: GOOD



✅ Task complete

→ Lock down builder module so regressions like FileTree missing never happen again.
